title: Practice 8: при- and у-: arriving, and leaving

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **уйти́** — **уходи́ть** — to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade. **уе́хать** — **уезжа́ть** — to go away, to drive off, to leave, to depart (by conveyance). **улете́ть** — **улета́ть** — to fly away, to depart (by flying); (figuratively) to be carried away or transported in thoughts or feelings. **убежа́ть** — **убега́ть** — to run away, to make off, to flee; to escape. **уплы́ть** — **уплыва́ть** — to swim away; to sail away. — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: As time goes on, grief fades away.
exercises.context: уйти́** — **уходи́ть — to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade.

exercises.why: These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: And what will be the result of that?
exercises.context: These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning.

exercises.q: Leave the door ajar when you go.
exercises.why: Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving. Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто… — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving. (DLI, Lesson 24)

exercises.why: With the carrying verbs: приносить — принести — to bring (on foot); привозить — привезти — to bring (by vehicle); приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead; уносить — унести — to take (carry) away; увозить — увезти — to take (haul) away; уводить — увести — to take (lead) away. — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: With the carrying verbs: приносить — принести — to bring (on foot); привозить — привезти — to bring (by vehicle); приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead; уносить — унести — to take (carry) away; увозить — увезти — to take (haul) away;…

exercises.why: **улете́ть** — **улета́ть** — to fly away, to depart (by flying); (figuratively) to be carried away or transported in thoughts or feelings. **убежа́ть** — **убега́ть** — to run away, to make off, to flee; to escape. **уплы́ть** — **уплыва́ть** — to swim away; to sail away. **унести́** — **уноси́ть** — to take away, to take off, to carry (away); (figuratively) to take (a life), to claim (a life). **увести́** — **уводи́ть** — to take away, to lead away, to withdraw (troops); to carry off, to lift. — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: Приходить and приезжать are not used to denote an action in progress. **при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- — Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. — в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.. **у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Приходить and приезжать are not used to denote an action in progress.

exercises.why: **прие́хать** — **приезжа́ть** — to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse); (past tense, plural only) to hit rock bottom. **прилете́ть** — **прилета́ть** — to fly (here), to arrive (by flying). **прибежа́ть** — **прибега́ть** — to come running. **приплы́ть** — **приплыва́ть** — to swim up, to come swimming, to sail up. **принести́** — **приноси́ть** — to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); to yield, to bear. — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: прие́хать** — **приезжа́ть — to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse); (past tense, plural only) to hit rock bottom.
